newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian spacecraft docks with Mir station.
newsitem.headline: Russian spacecraft docks with Mir station.

text.p: A Russian Soyuz TM-25 rocket docked with the Mir space station on Wednesday, bringing replacements for two cosmonauts who have been in orbit six months, a space official said.
The new crew -- two Russians and a German -- crossed over to Mir via transit hatches at around 8.22 p.m. (1722 GMT).
Television pictures showed the two crews chatting and sharing food.
"I feel fine and am keen to get on with the experiments that lie ahead," said the German cosmonaut, Reinhold Ewald.
Ewald, 40, is due to stay aboard Mir for 20 days before returning to Earth with Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri who have been aboard the station for six months.

Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin are scheduled to remain in space along with U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger, who began to work at the station on January 15. They are scheduled to return to Earth in June.

"Docking took place one minute late at 6.51 p.m. (1551 GMT)," an official at mission control in the northern Moscow suburb of Kaliningrad told Reuters by telephone. "It looks as though they switched to manual for the final manoeuvre."
Docking between the space station and the space craft is usually automatic.
The three cosmonauts aboard Soyuz blasted off from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan two days ago.
Ewald is flying under an agreement between Germany and Russia in which Germany will pay millions of dollars for the ride -- a welcome boost for the struggling Russian space industry.
Germany has said it considers Ewald's flight important as preparation for the international Alpha space station, assembly of which will start this year.
The 120-tonne Mir space station was launched in 1985 and is expected to be in use until 1999, when the Alpha space station would become the world's primary vehicle for long-term space endurance.
Mir has been manned continuously since September 1989.
